surrogate.note: The surrogate emulates the canonical Python engine (a calibrated cheap physics model), not a real plant. Held-out is an independent second Latin-hypercube draw (seed 67890, 480 points per machine, degenerate draws dropped), not a split of the training draw. R2 and MAPE are in original units, computed through onnxruntime on the shipped float32 graph (MAPE also on the int8 graph). Parity is the maximum absolute difference of the standardised outputs on the held-out draw, torch loaded with the weights read out of the float32 graph. Monotonicity: P80 does not fall by more than 0.001 mm as CSS opens, on 15 curves (16 settings across each machine's range at the 25%, 50% and 75% points of its other inputs).

anomaly.planted: One planted point per held-out point, its operating inputs moved outside that machine's training range and then run through the engine: by held-out index modulo 18, one of the six continuous inputs (CSS, throw, speed, feed x63, feed m, ore A*b) moved above its upper bound by half the range width (patterns 0 to 5), one moved below its lower bound to half the bound (6 to 11), or two neighbouring inputs moved, the first above and the second below (12 to 17); ore_wi follows the A*b rule. Points whose engine result has a non-finite feature are left out.
anomaly.note: Alarm threshold: 0.24454 (the 99th percentile of the training scores); a score above it, or a non-finite score, is an alarm. The envelope gate is the engine's rule check (out_of_envelope): on the synthetic lane it flags only physically implausible inputs (CSS at or above F80, a non-positive CSS or feed size), so a point that is physically plausible but outside the training range passes it; the autoencoder scores distance from the training manifold, the complementary check.
